title: RBAC v2: staged identity mapping reconciler, admin-override workflow, and audit-preserving cutover
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: perform a low-risk, audit-preserving migration from RBAC v1 -> RBAC v2 by implementing a staged identity mapping reconciler, a scoped admin-override workflow, and a telemetry-first cutover. This ticket covers the reconciler service (imap-reconcile), the admin-override UI and API guardrails, synthetic canary generation from customer permission matrices, and end-to-end audit forwarding for each change. We must ensure dual-write safety, prevent silent permission drops, and provide an immediate, observable rollback path. Deliverables: reconciler binary + operator CLI, admin-override endpoints + soft-lock audit tagging, canary dataset and automation, customer comms template and opt-in toggle, monitoring dashboards and SLO gates.
acceptance_criteria: imap-reconcile successfully replays and reconciles 1000 synthetic user permission permutations without divergence
Every admin-override action is tagged with an audit_soft_lock flag and emits structured audit events to the audit-stream and SIEM
Dual-write shadow mode runs for 72 hours with divergence <= 0.05% on sampled orgs before canary enablement
Canary rollout automation supports per-org opt-in and automatic rollback on error-rate or permission-delta threshold breaches
Documentation: runbook, API schema changes, and customer-facing comms published in Confluence and linked in this ticket
runbook_steps: Enable imap-reconcile in read-only shadow mode for the first 50 internal orgs (shadow=true)
Run nightly reconciliation for 3 days; collect diff artifacts in gs://redwood-rbac-reconcile/nightly/<date>/
Promote reconciler to dual-write mode (writes to v2 plus v1) with change-tracing enabled and audit_soft_lock header set
Launch synthetic canaries (generated from canary-generator) against a staging cluster and validate no permission regressions
Open per-org opt-in toggle in Console under Admin -> RBAC v2 -> Migration -> Opt-in; enable for wave-1 orgs
Monitor dashboards for permission_delta_count, admin_override_count, reconciliation_latency, and audit_event_delivery_rate
If permission_delta_count > 10 for any org in wave: automatically revert opt-in for that org and create incident ENG-ROLLBACK-<org>
rollback_plan: Instant rollback: flip per-org opt-in toggle off; imap-reconcile marks last known-good mapping and emits revert event
Data rollback: run backfill job imap-reconcile --mode=revert --org=<org> to restore v2->v1 parity for affected principal sets
Operational rollback: disable dual-write at the routing layer (feature flag: rbac.v2.dual_write=false) and verify requests land on v1
Communications rollback: notify customers via the pre-approved rollback template and post incident summary within 24 hours
Postmortem: collect audit_stream snapshots and reconciliation diffs, then run root cause analysis within 5 business days

customer_comms: Subject: Optional RBAC migration (RBAC v2) - safe opt-in available

Hello <Customer Admin>,

We are beginning an optional migration to RBAC v2 which improves permission performance and auditability. You can opt in per-organization from the Console (Admin -> RBAC -> Migration). During opt-in we will run reconciliation and preserve full audit trails. If you opt in we will: run a non-destructive reconciliation, tag any admin-driven changes with audit_soft_lock, and keep your org on v1 as a fallback for 7 days.

If you do not opt in we will continue to support v1. Please contact support@redwood.ai to schedule a migration window or request assistance.
Opt-in CLI: rbacctl migrate --org <org_id> --wave wave-1 --notify true

Rollback notice template: We have temporarily reverted RBAC v2 opt-in for your org due to detected permission diffs above threshold. Your production permissions should remain unaffected; our team is investigating and will follow up within 24 hours.
risk_assessment: High: changing authorization surface is high-risk. Mitigations: strict shadow mode, dual-write with trace ids, audit_soft_lock tagging, synthetic canaries, per-org opt-in, and automated rollback triggers. Residual risks include complex SAML mappings and third-party provisioning delays. Security review required before any org-scale rollout.
notes: Admin-override design: any manual change via Console or API must include a justification string and be rate-limited to 5 changes/hour per admin; the justification is stored in the audit event and surfaced as audit_soft_lock=true.
SAML mapping canonicalizer: canonicalizeNameID and normalize attribute lists before reconciliation to avoid mapping churn for identity providers that include transient attributes.
Observability: create a synthetic alert that fires if reconciliation job latency doubles or if audit_event_delivery_rate drops below 99.5%.
Privacy: ensure audit events forwarded to external SIEM redacts PII per Data Classification policy; include redaction step in reconciler pipeline.
